# Frozen attribution regression fixtures (SMP-4.6)

These JSON files are **frozen, checked-in expected values** — they are never
regenerated by `tests/test_catalog_attribution_regression.py` at run time.
Each was produced once by actually calling the real service code against a
fixed, deterministic input, then hand-frozen to disk. The regression test
re-derives the same output from the same fixed inputs and diffs it against
these files; a silent shape change in the underlying code (a renamed key, a
folded tri-state, a dropped field) makes the diff fail loudly.

If a fixture ever needs to change because of an intentional, reviewed shape
change, regenerate it deliberately and say so in the commit message — do not
let a test helper regenerate it automatically, or it stops being able to
catch drift.

| File | Freezes |
|---|---|
| `catalog_coverage_tristate.json` | `catalog_service.attribution_coverage()`'s tri-state coverage block, with three cardinalities (2/1/4) deliberately distinct from each other so a future collapse of `absent` into `not_yet_assessed` (or vice versa) cannot hide behind coincidentally-equal counts. |
| `resolved_source_with_attribution_summary.json` | `export_service._resolve_source()`'s full resolved-source dict for a source card carrying `authors`/`doi`/`publisher`/`version`/`attribution_summary` (the SMP-1.4/SMP-4.4 fields). |
| `resolved_source_legacy_pre_change.json` | The same function's output for a source card predating source-metadata-propagation-v1 entirely — no `authors`/`doi`/`publisher`/`version` on `source`, no `attribution_summary` key on the card meta at all. Proves the change is additive: the five keys are still present in the resolved dict, just `null`. |
| `source_attribution_record.json` | `attribution_triage.mint_attribution_record().as_dict()` — the authoritative `source_attribution` record shape (M2's new top-level entity), for one fixed set of constructor inputs. `attribution_id` is content-derived (no wall-clock read), so this is exactly reproducible. |
